findings.reason:
Two-part claim; split verdict but the player-visible defect is real.

(1) "DOM reports bfExhausted=0" is a HARNESS false positive, not a UI bug: monkey-drive.ts:93 counts `[id^="bf-"] .card.card--exhausted, .bf-zone .card.card--exhausted`, but the UI renders battlefield units under `#battlefieldRow .battlefield .bf-units` (board.js:119-139, gameplay.html:155) — no element has id starting "bf-" or class .bf-zone, so this count is always 0. card.js:151-153 does add `exhausted card--exhausted` whenever meta.exhausted is true, and the trace shows the client gameState had meta.exhausted=true for Ravenbloom Student, so the class was in the DOM.

(2) The clipping is real and source-traceable. 36.png shows Back-Alley Bar's player-side units as a ~15px sliver. Cause: gameplay.css:1143-1158 `.bf-units { flex: 1 1 56px; min-height:0; overflow-y:auto }` inside `.bf-body` (1108-1118, min-height:0) inside `.battlefield { overflow:hidden }` (915-928), all within `.battlefield-row { flex:2; min-height:180px }` (109-121). With header+divider+two unit rows in 180px logical, each .bf-units row gets ~45px while `.bf-units .card { height:126px }` (490-494), so even a single row of units is cut to its top edge and the 90°-rotated exhausted state cannot be seen without scrolling a tiny strip — contrary to the CSS comment's own intent ("keeps the first row visible") and DESIGN.md:12.

findings.what: Lotus Trap's 'Double all damage that would be dealt to it this turn' has no effect
findings.expected: After Lotus Trap resolves on Magma Wurm (8 Might), Falling Star's 'Deal 3' should deal 6 damage to it
findings.observed: Wurm received grantedKeywords=[{keyword:'DoubleIncomingDamage',duration:'turn'}] but Falling Star dealt exactly 3 damage (meta.damage=3). Reproduced twice (cast normally before the damage spell, and cast as a Reaction on top of Falling Star in the chain). grep shows 'DoubleIncomingDamage' is only referenced in packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/lotus-trap.ts — the engine's damage pipeline never consumes the keyword.
findings.reason: Repo-wide grep for "DoubleIncomingDamage" across packages/ and apps/ finds exactly one hit: the card definition packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/lotus-trap.ts:16 (grant-keyword effect). The engine damage pipeline in packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/damage.ts:260-325 iterates hits and applies `amount` verbatim (addCounter at :316, meta.damage = priorDamage + amount at :320) with only take-damage replacement checks (prevent/alt-effect) — no keyword lookup or multiplier anywhere. So the granted keyword is inert and Falling Star deals 3, not 6.

findings.what: 'When this is played ... draw 1' does not trigger
findings.expected: Playing Scrapheap (hand 6, deck 35) should leave hand at 6 (5 + draw 1) and deck 34
findings.observed: playGear resolved ('dev equipped Scrapheap'), no chain item/trigger, hand 5, deck 35 unchanged
findings.reason: /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/scrapheap.ts:4-14 defines Scrapheap with only rulesText ("When this is played, discarded, or killed, draw 1.") and no `abilities` field. The engine only executes structured `abilities[]` (compare bandle-tree.ts:16,27 which sets `abilities`); coverage-check.ts:129 explicitly flags this class ("cards PLAYED with rulesText but NO abilities[] (effect never fires)"). So no triggered ability is registered on play, matching the observed hand 5 / deck 35.

findings.what: 'When this is ... killed, draw 1' does not trigger
findings.expected: Detonate (Kill a gear. Its controller draws 2) on Scrapheap should net 3 draws (2 from Detonate + 1 from Scrapheap)
findings.observed: Scrapheap moved to trash, player-1 deck 35->33 and hand +2 only (Detonate's draws); no Scrapheap trigger on chain
findings.reason: Scrapheap has no hand-written abilities (riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/scrapheap.ts) so it is enriched via parseAbilities, which maps "When this is played, discarded, or killed," to synthetic event "play-discard-or-die-self" (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/trigger-patterns.ts:271). The engine's triggerMatchesEvent splits trigger.event on "-or-" (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/trigger-matcher.ts:218-228) yielding ["play-discard","die-self"], neither of which equals the fired "die" (or "play-self"/"discard") event, so the trigger never matches. Confirmed by src/__tests__/cards/ogn-182-298.test.ts:58 test.failing (killed branch) passing as expected-failing when run.

findings.what: 'When this is ... discarded, draw 1' does not trigger
findings.expected: Discarding Scrapheap to Chemtech Enforcer's 'discard 1' should draw 1 (deck 34->33, hand stays 5)
findings.observed: Scrapheap went to trash via reveal-and-pick discard; deck stayed 34, hand 6->5, no trigger
findings.reason: Scrapheap's ability is parsed (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/trigger-patterns.ts:271) into the synthetic trigger event "play-discard-or-die-self". The engine matcher (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/trigger-matcher.ts:218-228) splits compound events on "-or-", yielding ["play-discard","die-self"] — neither equals the engine's "discard" (nor "die"/"play-self") event, so triggerMatchesEvent returns false and no draw fires. Verified: registry shows abilities=[{trigger:{event:"play-discard-or-die-self",on:"self"},effect:{type:"draw",amount:1}}], and the existing test.failing case "discarded from hand by your own effect draws 1" in src/__tests__/cards/ogn-182-298.test.ts still passes as failing (bun test: 6 pass). Fix: emit event "play-self-or-discard-or-die" in the parser pattern (or map it in EVENT_MAP/split normalization).

findings.what: Gearhead's 'Each Equipment attached to me gives double its base Might bonus' is not applied
findings.expected: Gearhead (3) with Doran's Blade attached (base bonus +2) should be 3 + 2*2 = 7 Might
findings.observed: After equipCard (Doran's Blade -> Gearhead), meta showed equippedWith=[Doran's Blade], equipmentMightBonus=2, staticMightBonus=0; card tile displayed 5 Might. Still 5 after a subsequent standardMove (recalc opportunity).
findings.reason: Reproduced with the harness: scenario with Gearhead (sfd-068-221) in base + Skyfall (+2) gear; after `equipCard` + settle, game.state("gh") shows might=5, staticMightBonus=0, equippedWith=["sky"] (expected 7). The parser emits the correct static ({type:"modify-might", source:"equipment", multiplier:2} — static-parser.ts:817-834) and static-abilities.ts:518-537 does implement the (multiplier-1)×base doubling, but it never runs after equipping: the equipCard reducer (game-definition/moves/equipment.ts:112-151) only calls fireTriggers({type:"attach-equipment"}) at line 142 directly — not dispatchEvent / cleanupAndFireDeaths — and equipmentMoves are not wrapped in withPostMoveCleanup, and "attach-equipment" is absent from EVENT_TYPES_NEEDING_RECALC (events/dispatcher.ts:82-112). So recalculateStaticEffects is not invoked and staticMightBonus stays 0 → 3+2=5. Note: with current code a subsequent standardMove (movement.ts is wrapped in withPostMoveCleanup) does recalc to 7, so the "still 5 after standardMove" sub-observation no longer reproduces (the static-abilities.ts handling landed in cbd38e3 today), but the primary defect — Gearhead reads 5 not 7 immediately after equipCard — is confirmed.

findings.what: No player-facing way to Equip a standalone Equipment on board to a unit
findings.expected: With Doran's Blade in base, Gearhead in base and body power available, an Equip action ([body]: Attach this to a unit you control) should be offered (activateAbility / equipCard in available moves, or via UI)
findings.observed: enumerateMoves listed no equipCard/activateAbility for the equipment; playGear with chosenTargetId=Gearhead also left it unattached in base. Only the non-enumerated raw REST 'equipCard' move could attach it.
findings.reason: The only engine path that attaches an equipment already on board is `equipCard` (packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/equipment.ts:50-151), which defines only `condition` + `reducer` and no `enumerator` (and pays no Equip cost). Core enumerateMoves treats enumerator-less moves as an invalid NO_ENUMERATOR placeholder (packages/core/src/engine/rule-engine.ts:970-984), so equipCard never appears as a valid available move. The `activateAbility` enumerator only collects abilities with `ability.type === "activated"` (chain/activate-ability.ts:101-105), while the parsed Equip ability is `{ type: "keyword", keyword: "Equip", cost }` (e.g. riftbound-cards the-zero-drive.ts:26; only consumer is the Weaponmaster pending-choice at pending-choice.ts:188), so no activateAbility entry is generated for Doran's Blade. UI drag-drop only handles equipment dragged from hand via playGear (apps/riftbound-app/public/js/gameplay/drag-drop.js:333-349, gated on `dragState.zone === "hand"`), and play-gear.ts reducer only passes chosenTargetId to deductCost without attaching. Hence no player-facing Equip action for a standalone equipment in base.

findings.what: Yi's +4 Might is applied unconditionally, ignoring the 'While you have 8+ runes' condition
findings.expected: With only 2 runes on board (Runes 2/2, turn 1), Yi should be its printed 4 Might
findings.observed: Immediately after playUnit on turn 1 with 2 runes in pool, meta.staticMightBonus=4 and the board tile displayed 8 Might
findings.reason: yi-meditative.ts declares no `abilities`, so enrich-cards.ts parses rulesText; parser output (verified via bun) is a static ability with condition `{type:"custom", text:"While you have 8+ runes"}` and effect modify-might +4 self. evaluateCondition (static-abilities.ts:105-316) has no "custom"/rune-count case, and the `default` branch at static-abilities.ts:312-315 returns true ("Unknown condition — default to true"), so recalculateStaticEffects applies staticMightBonus=4 regardless of rune count.

findings.what: 'I have +1 [Might] for each friendly gear' does not scale with gear count
findings.expected: With 2 friendly gear on board Ornn should be 4+2=6 Might; with 3 friendly gear 4+3=7
findings.observed: meta.staticMightBonus stayed at 1 and UI 'Effective Might' showed 5 with 2 friendly gear (2x Serrated Dirk, one attached) and still 5 after a 3rd gear (Hand Hammer + Seal of Rage + Sun Disc in first run). Bonus is a flat +1 regardless of gear count.
findings.reason: Ornn (sfd-085-221) has no hand-authored abilities; enrich-cards.ts parses rulesText into a static ability `{type:"modify-might", amount:1, per:"friendly gear", target:"self"}` (verified by running parseAbilities). The engine's applyStaticEffect in riftbound-engine/src/abilities/static-abilities.ts:492-517 only computes `amount` from a numeric literal, `cardsInTrash`, or `score`; it never reads `effect.per` (no reference to `per` anywhere in static-abilities.ts or the abilities/ dir). So `amount = 1` is applied flat at line 547-551 (`staticMightBonus: current + targetAmount`), regardless of friendly gear count — matching the observed staticMightBonus=1 / Effective Might 5.

findings.what: Weaponmaster prompt not offered when the only Equipment in play is Hand Hammer (ven-027-166)
findings.expected: Hand Hammer's text is '[Equip] [calm]' (an Equipment), so playing Ornn with Hand Hammer in base should raise the weaponmaster-equip choice (equip for [rainbow] less = free)
findings.observed: No pendingChoice/chain after playing Ornn with Hand Hammer + Seal of Rage in base. Same flow with Serrated Dirk (sfd-009-221) DID prompt. Hand Hammer surfaces as type 'gear' (not 'equipment') and its parsed abilities are [null] in ven.json, so the engine doesn't see it as Equipment. Root cause is Hand Hammer card data, surfaced via Ornn.
findings.reason: Reproduced: playing Ornn (sfd-085-221) with Hand Hammer (ven-027-166) in base yields no weaponmaster-equip pick (decision falls straight back to main-phase action), while the identical setup with Serrated Dirk (sfd-009-221) yields the `weaponmaster-equip` pick. Root cause: play-unit.ts:572 gates Weaponmaster options on `registry.get(id)?.cardType === "equipment"`. Serrated Dirk has a hand-authored def (riftbound-cards/src/cards/sfd/serrated-dirk.ts:6 `cardType: "equipment"`), but VEN has no .ts defs — Hand Hammer flows through adaptJsonCard (riftbound-cards/src/data/all-cards.ts:809 `cardType: c.cardType`) which passes ven.json's `"cardType": "gear"` through unchanged, and enrich-cards.ts never remaps gear-with-Equip to equipment. Runtime registry confirms ven-027-166 cardType="gear" (abilities do get re-parsed to Equip [calm], so the `[null]` detail is cosmetic; the cardType is the actual discriminator). Card-data layer bug in Hand Hammer / VEN JSON adaptation, surfaced via Ornn.

findings.what: 'Each player kills one of their gear' implemented as caster kills one target gear of any player
findings.expected: On resolution every player with gear loses exactly one of THEIR OWN gear (each player choosing among their own if several); caster should not be able to pick an opponent's gear, and opponent's gear should die too
findings.observed: Move enumeration offered playSpell targets = all gear on board incl. opponent's Gold token. Cast #1 (p1 has Seal of Rage + Sun Disc, p2 has Gold) targeting own Seal of Rage: only Seal of Rage went to trash; p2's Gold stayed in base, no prompt for p2. Cast #2 targeting p2's Gold: Gold was killed and p1's own Sun Disc survived. Chain item effect was {type:kill, player:each, target:{type:gear}} but resolved as single-target kill.
findings.reason: Parser (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-damage.ts:139-149) emits {type:"kill", player:"each", target:{type:"gear"}} for "Each player kills one of their gear." But the engine handler handle_kill (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/kill.ts:8-29) never reads effect.player — it just calls getTargetIds(effect, ctx) and trashes those targets, i.e. a plain single-target kill on the caster-chosen target. Grep of the engine for `"each"` shows player:"each" fan-out is implemented only in draw.ts:10, discard.ts:18, channel.ts:13 (and grant-keyword) — not kill. Since the target descriptor {type:"gear"} carries no controller restriction, play-spell enumeration offers every gear on board (including opponent's), and resolution kills only that one card with no per-player choice. Matches observed behavior.

findings.what: [Ambush] not honored for Rengar in hand — cannot be played as a Reaction to a battlefield where player has units
findings.expected: With friendly Pouty Poro at battlefield-player-1-bf-ogn-277-298 during opponent's turn (neutral-open, and again while p1 held showdown focus), playUnit Rengar -> that battlefield should be offered/accepted (rule 822.1.b), exactly as it was for Inferna (unl-002-219, printed Ambush) in the same state
findings.observed: enumerateMoves listed playUnit->battlefield-player-1-bf for both Inferna copies but nothing for Rengar; direct playUnit {location:battlefield-player-1-bf-ogn-277-298} returned CONDITION_FAILED. Card def encodes Ambush as static {type:'grant-keyword',keyword:'Ambush',target:'self'}; CardDefinitionRegistry.hasKeyword only checks keywords[] / abilities of type 'keyword', so play-unit.ts sees hasAmbush=false for the in-hand card
findings.reason: packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/rengar-trophy-hunter.ts:16-33 encodes Ambush only as `{type:'static', effect:{type:'grant-keyword', keyword:'Ambush', target:'self'}}` (no `keywords` array, no `type:'keyword'` ability); this TS override is what all-cards.ts:690 exports (the JSON's `{type:'keyword',keyword:'Ambush'}` is superseded). CardDefinitionRegistry.hasKeyword (riftbound-engine/src/operations/card-lookup.ts:122-133) checks only `def.keywords` and abilities with `type === 'keyword'`, and toLookupPayload (harness/card-pool.ts:114,123) passes abilities/keywords through unchanged. So play-unit.ts:103 computes hasAmbush=false and play-unit.ts:141 (`targetIsBattlefield && !hasAmbush -> return false`) rejects the reaction-timed battlefield play, matching the observed CONDITION_FAILED while printed-keyword Inferna passes.

In play-unit.ts condition (lines 116-177), an enemy-controlled battlefield target matches none of: conquered-only (118), controlled-bf (123: requires targetBf.controller === playerId), open-bf (128: requires !targetBf.controller). findings.what: 'Give a friendly unit +3 Might this turn' is not applied
findings.expected: Chosen friendly unit (Rengar, 6 Might) should become 9 Might for the turn before the damage exchange and remain 9 until end of turn
findings.observed: After resolution Rengar's might stayed 6 (no mightModifier in meta, UI shows 6); enemy Pit Crew received 6 damage not 9. Registered ability is only {type:'fight', attacker:friendly unit, defender:enemy unit} — no modify-might/onAttacker step (matches the known test.failing in ogs-008-024.test.ts)
findings.reason: Card def (riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogs/gentlemens-duel.ts) has no explicit abilities; they come from the text parser. In parser/impl/effects.ts:146 parseEffect(cleaned) runs on the whole text BEFORE the '. Then ' split at line 154, and parseFightEffect (parser/impl/effects-damage.ts:216) matches only on the end-anchored regex /deal damage equal to their Mights to each other\.?$/ — so the full string 'Give a friendly unit +3 [Might] this turn. Then choose an enemy unit. They deal damage…' matches as a single fight effect with default friendly/enemy targets (lines 222-234), discarding the +3 Might clause. Verified by running parseAbilities on the card text: output is exactly {effect:{type:'fight',attacker:{controller:'friendly',type:'unit'},defender:{controller:'enemy',type:'unit'}},timing:'action',type:'spell'} — no modify-might step. Matches test.failing in riftbound-engine/src/__tests__/cards/ogs-008-024.test.ts.

findings.what: playSpell accepted with no targets and auto-picked units at resolution, bypassing the choice and Deflect
findings.expected: Spell requires choosing a friendly and an enemy unit; when the only enemy unit (Pouty Poro, Deflect) cannot legally be chosen (p1 had no spare power for the Deflect surcharge) the play should be rejected, or at minimum the caster should be prompted and Deflect cost charged
findings.observed: Enumerator offered no playSpell move (UI showed card unplayable), but REST playSpell {cardId, playerId} with no targets returned success, paid 6+body, put the spell on chain with no targets, and on resolution the fight handler silently picked Rengar and the Deflect Poro (Poro killed, Rengar took 2) with no pendingChoice and no Deflect payment
findings.reason: Reproduced with harness: P1 (6 energy + 1 body, no spare power), friendly 4-Might unit, only enemy unit = Pouty Poro (ogn-013-298, Deflect). game.p1.can("cast","duel") === false (enumerator's [attacker,defender] pairs at play-spell.ts:512-530 are filtered out by condition because canAffordCard with targets includes the Deflect rainbow surcharge). But raw playSpell {cardId, playerId} with no targets returned ok: paid 6+body, spell went to chain with targets undefined, and after settle Poro was in trash, Rengar had 2 damage, no pendingChoice, resources unchanged beyond base cost. Root cause: playSpell.condition (play-spell.ts:82-339) never requires targets for a `fight` effect — canAffordCard at :173-188 computes Deflect from context.params.targets (undefined → 0 surcharge, cost.ts:1016 getDeflectSurcharge), spellEffectHasLegalTargets at :235 only checks existence, and the single-target validation at :249-268 is skipped when targets is absent. At resolution abilities/effects/fight.ts:19-31 falls back to resolveTarget(...)[0] for attacker/defender when boundTargets are missing, silently auto-picking without a prompt or Deflect payment.

findings.what: Astral Heron's triggered effect 'your next card costs [2][rainbow][rainbow] less' is unimplemented (resolves as a raw-text no-op).
findings.expected: After the trigger resolves, the next card played should cost 2 energy less (and up to 2 power of any domain less). Shipyard Skulker (cost 3) should have cost 1: energy 8 -> 7.
findings.observed: Trigger fired and went on the chain with effect {"type":"raw","text":"your next card costs :rb_energy_2::rb_rune_rainbow::rb_rune_rainbow: less."}; after resolving it, hand still showed Shipyard Skulker cost 3 and playing it deducted full cost: energy 8 -> 5. No cost reduction applied.
findings.reason: Card def ven.json:1577-1579 has rulesText but abilities:[]/parseSuccess:false; the runtime parser matches the trigger via trigger-patterns.ts:373-379 ("When you play your first card each turn") but no effect parser handles "your next card costs [2][rainbow][rainbow] less" (only "I cost X less" static/self cost-reduction exists: effect-keyword-parser.ts:357-363, static-parser.ts), so the effect falls back to {type:"raw"}. Engine executeEffect (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts:150-156) has no EFFECT_HANDLERS["raw"] entry and silently no-ops. Existing ruling test astral-heron-8cedb5e8fc134531.test.ts encodes this exact bug as test.failing ("engine applies no discount") and it currently passes (i.e., the discount is indeed not applied) when run with bun test.

findings.what: Icathian Rain resolves only one 'Deal 2 to a unit' instance instead of six
findings.expected: Six separate 'Deal 2 to a unit' instances (12 total damage), each with its own target choice (same or different units) — e.g. a prompt per instance or a 6-target selection
findings.observed: playSpell moves enumerate a single target (targets:[one id]); chain item is a single {type:'damage',amount:2,target:{type:'unit'}}; after resolving, the chosen unit (Flame Chompers, 3 might) had damage=2 and the spell went to trash with no further prompts/pendingChoice for the remaining 5 instances. Other units took 0.
findings.reason: Enriched card def for ogn-248-298 (verified via getAllCards()) has six separate {type:'spell', effect:{type:'damage',amount:2,target:{type:'unit'}}} abilities. The engine only ever uses the first: play-spell.ts:956 `const spellAbility = abilities.find((a) => a.type === "spell")` stores that single effect on the chain (addToChain at :984), and the enumerator/condition (play-spell.ts:210, :411, :829) and resolve fallback (chain/resolve.ts:91) likewise use `.find`. No code folds multiple spell abilities into a sequence, so only one 'Deal 2 to a unit' instance with one target is resolved; the other five are dropped.

findings.what: Bandle Soldier's [Level 3] condition on 'I enter ready' is ignored — it enters ready even with 0 XP
findings.expected: With player XP < 3 the unit should enter exhausted like any other unit (rule 143.4); only with 3+ XP should it enter ready
findings.observed: At xp=0, playUnit put Bandle Soldier in base with meta.exhausted=false (rendered upright, standardMove immediately offered), while control unit Mister Root played right after entered exhausted=true. Parser emits {type:'static',effect:{type:'enter-ready'},condition:{type:'while-level',threshold:3}} but staticEnterReadyApplies/evaluateEnterReadyCondition in moves/play/cost.ts has no 'while-level' case (returns undefined -> treated as unconditional true).
findings.reason: Parser emits {type:'static',effect:{type:'enter-ready'},condition:{type:'while-level',threshold:3}} for unl-151-219 (verified via parseAbilities). In packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/play/cost.ts, evaluateEnterReadyCondition (lines 77-129) handles only not/score-within/this-turn/opponent-controls; 'while-level' falls to default -> undefined. staticEnterReadyApplies line 70 (`!condition || evaluate(...) !== false`) treats undefined as true, so Bandle Soldier enters ready regardless of XP.

findings.what: "Units can't move to base" is not enforced. With Minotaur Reckoner in play (base), a readied friendly Chemtech Enforcer at a battlefield was offered `standardMove {destination:"base"}` in the available-moves list and the move executed successfully (log: "dev moved Chemtech Enforcer to base").
findings.expected: While Reckoner is in play, no unit may move to base: standardMove to base should not be enumerated and should be rejected if attempted.
findings.observed: Server state showed the static aura working at the data level (both units carried grantedKeywords:[{keyword:"NoMoveToBase",duration:"static"}]), but the move to base was enumerated and succeeded. `grep NoMoveToBase` in packages/riftbound-engine/src finds no reader — the custom keyword granted by the card (packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/sfd/minotaur-reckoner.ts) is never consulted by standard-move validation/enumeration.
findings.reason: minotaur-reckoner.ts:16-25 grants custom keyword "NoMoveToBase" via static grant-keyword, but `grep -rn NoMoveToBase packages/riftbound-engine/src` returns nothing. standard-move.ts condition (lines 54-95) only checks zone/owner/exhausted/surcharge for toBase moves, and the enumerator (lines 170-202) unconditionally offers destination:"base" for every ready battlefield unit. No reader of the keyword exists, so the restriction is never enforced.

findings.what: "When you play me from face down on your turn, you may move an enemy unit at a different location to my battlefield" never triggers.
findings.expected: After revealHidden (play from facedown) on my own turn with an enemy unit (Shadow Order Disciple, controller player-2) sitting in base, an optional prompt/chain item should appear letting me move that enemy unit to Evelynn's battlefield.
findings.observed: revealHidden succeeded (Evelynn entered battlefield-player-1-bf-ogn-275-298 exhausted) but chain=null, pendingChoice=null, no opt-in prompt, and the enemy unit stayed in base. Root cause in engine: revealHidden (moves/play/hide.ts) fires only 'play-self' (with fromHiddenAt) and 'play-card' events; nothing ever emits a 'play-from-hidden' event and trigger-matcher EVENT_MAP has no entry for it, so the card's trigger {event:"play-from-hidden", on:"self"} can never match.
findings.reason: Card def (riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/evelynn-entrancing.ts:29-33) uses trigger {event:"play-from-hidden", on:"self"}. revealHidden in game-definition/moves/play/hide.ts:356-361 fires only {type:"play-self", fromHiddenAt} and {type:"play-card"}; grep shows no emitter of "play-from-hidden" anywhere in engine src (only a test comment in __tests__/cards/ogn-167-298.test.ts:69 acknowledging the gap). trigger-matcher.ts EVENT_MAP (87-118) has no play-from-hidden entry and triggerMatchesEvent (213-230) only aliases beginning-phase/recycle-cards-to-deck/typed play-<cardType>, so a play-self event never matches a "play-from-hidden" trigger. The ability can never fire.

findings.what: [Level 3] 'enter ready' clause not applied when playing Scorchclaw with 3+ XP
findings.expected: With player-1 at 4 XP (Level 3 active), Scorchclaw played to base should enter ready (rulesText: 'I have +1 [Might] and enter ready. (While you have 3+ XP, get the effect.)')
findings.observed: Played via playUnit at XP=4: card meta.exhausted=true, DOM class 'card--exhausted' (the +1 Might half of the same ability DID apply: staticMightBonus=1, Effective Might 4). Root cause: engine cost.ts staticEnterReadyApplies()/hasStaticEffect() only match a static ability whose top-level effect.type==='enter-ready'; the parser emits this ability as {type:'static', condition:{type:'while-level',threshold:3}, effect:{type:'sequence', effects:[modify-might, enter-ready]}}, so the nested enter-ready is never seen (and the while-level condition is not evaluated by evaluateEnterReadyCondition either).
findings.reason: Parser output for Scorchclaw (verified by running parseAbilities on its rulesText) is {type:'static', condition:{type:'while-level',threshold:3}, effect:{type:'sequence', effects:[{type:'modify-might',...},{type:'enter-ready',...}]}}. In packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/play/cost.ts:63-69, staticEnterReadyApplies() reads only the top-level ability.effect.type and `continue`s when it !== 'enter-ready' — no sequence unwrapping — so it returns false; hasStaticEffect() (cost.ts:32-44) has the same top-level-only check. play-unit.ts:525 uses staticEnterReadyApplies to decide entersReady, so the unit enters exhausted. evaluateEnterReadyCondition (cost.ts:77-130) also has no 'while-level' case (falls to default undefined). By contrast static-abilities.ts:694-697 does unwrap `sequence` effects, which is why the +1 Might half applies while enter-ready does not.

findings.what: Static 'My Might is increased by your points' does nothing on the VEN reprint
findings.expected: With player-1 at 1 victory point, Draven (base Might 3) at the battlefield should have effective Might 4 (staticMightBonus +1).
findings.observed: After conquering Aspirant's Climb (players.player-1.victoryPoints = 1), Draven's meta had no staticMightBonus/mightModifier and might stayed 3; UI showed no buff badge. Root cause: the loaded def for ven-172-166 has no `abilities` at all (ven.json entry has abilities:[] / parseSuccess:false and the parser can't handle this text), whereas the OGN printing ogn-028-298 carries a hand-authored static {type:'modify-might', amount:{score:'self'}, target:'self'}. The VEN reprint never inherits it.
findings.reason: ven.json:4714-4734 defines ven-172-166 with rulesText "My Might is increased by your points.", abilities:[], parseSuccess:false. adaptJsonCard (all-cards.ts:805-807) turns [] into undefined, so enrichCard (enrich-cards.ts:22-33) re-parses rulesText, but parseAbilities returns {success:false,"Could not parse ability text"} (verified by running the parser via bun). Result: getCardRegistry().get("ven-172-166").abilities === undefined, while ogn-028-298 gets the hand-authored static modify-might {amount:{score:'self'}} from cards/ogn/draven-showboat.ts:12-21. There is no cards/ven/ override directory and no name-based reprint inheritance in all-cards.ts/enrich-cards.ts, so the VEN printing has no static ability and gets no Might bonus from points.

findings.what: Reveal top rune of rune deck then recycle it does not happen
findings.expected: On attack-trigger resolution the top rune of player-1's rune deck is revealed (log/UI) and then recycled to the bottom of the rune deck, changing deck order
findings.observed: Across 4 runs the rune deck order was byte-identical before and after the trigger fully resolved (e.g. top '10-ogn-166' stayed on top, bottom unchanged), no reveal log entry or reveal UI; card def models this as look(rune-deck)+recycle(target rune from board) and neither has any observable effect
findings.reason: Card def (twisted-fate-gambler.ts:22-31) models the reveal as {type:"look", from:"rune-deck"} + {type:"recycle", from:"board", target:{type:"rune"}}. Both are no-ops in the engine: (1) look.ts:23-28 only maps "deck"->"mainDeck" and otherwise passes `from` verbatim; the engine zone is "runeDeck" (setup.ts:265, resources.ts:57) and no "rune-deck" alias exists anywhere in riftbound-engine/src, so getCardsInZone("rune-deck") yields nothing, topN is empty and the handler returns at look.ts:28 without setting any reveal pendingChoice. (2) recycle.ts:59-61 returns early unless target is self/unit/gear (comment at :53 explicitly says rune recycles are not handled), and :75-77 additionally skips rune cardType. So no reveal, no recycle, rune deck order unchanged — matches observation.

findings.what: Effect branch is a free player choice instead of being determined by the revealed rune's domain
findings.expected: Exactly one branch executes automatically based on the revealed rune's domain (fury/mind/order); with a Chaos rune on top (2 of the runs) nothing should happen; with a Fury rune on top only the fury damage branch should apply
findings.observed: Engine presented pendingChoice type 'choose-mode' with options fury/mind/order every time; player could pick Draw 1 or Stun with a Chaos or Fury rune on top and the chosen branch executed (hand 5->6 for mind; enemy stunned for order)
findings.reason: Card def /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/twisted-fate-gambler.ts:32-76 models the domain-gated switch as an unconditioned `type: "choice"` with options fury/mind/order (comment at lines 15-16 admits it is "approximating the actual domain-gated switch"). No option carries a condition on the revealed rune's domain, and the preceding `look` (line 22-26) does not bind the revealed rune for later gating. Engine handler /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/choice.ts:15-31 turns any >=2-option choice into a player-facing `choose-mode` pendingChoice listing all option indices, so the player freely picks any branch (including with a Chaos or Fury rune on top), matching the observed behavior.

findings.what: Fresh Beans' triggered ability never fires when a unit is played during a showdown
findings.expected: With Fresh Beans ready in base and a showdown in progress (my focus), playing units (Recruit the Vanguard -> 'Play four 1 Might Recruit unit tokens'; rule 350.2: tokens are Played) should trigger 'you may exhaust this to draw 1' — an optional prompt/pendingChoice, and on accept Fresh Beans exhausts and hand +1
findings.observed: 4 Recruit unit tokens entered base during the showdown (passShowdownFocus still available, UI banner 'Showdown in progress — your focus'); Fresh Beans stayed exhausted:false, no chain item, no pendingChoice, hand size unchanged (6). Root cause in engine: abilities/trigger-matcher.ts restriction `case "during-showdown": return false` (TODO) — the parsed trigger (event play-unit + restriction during-showdown from trigger-patterns.ts) can never match.
findings.reason: Fresh Beans (unl-011-219) rulesText parses via trigger-patterns.ts:278-283 to event play-unit with restrictions [{type:"during-showdown"}]. trigger-matcher.ts:171-173 handles `case "during-showdown": return false;` unconditionally (TODO: showdown state not exposed), so the restriction can never be satisfied and the triggered ability never fires, matching the observed no-prompt/no-exhaust behavior.

findings.what: A move that throws over the game WebSocket kills the server-side game session
findings.expected: A thrown move condition should be reported as a failed move (like the REST path's 500) and the game should remain
findings.observed: Sending the same Defy playSpell via the browser WS (executeMove) -> net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET on the socket, then GET /api/game/<id>/state returns 'Game not found' and WS reconnect gets 404; window.__rbGameId becomes null. Via REST the game survived the 500. Reproduced 3 times.
findings.reason: WS move path calls `session.engine.executeMove(...)` at apps/riftbound-app/server/ws-game.ts:90 with no try/catch (nor any in server.ts:98-115 websocket.message). In the engine, `checkMoveCondition` runs at packages/core/src/engine/rule-engine.ts:414, OUTSIDE the try block that starts at rule-engine.ts:567, so a throwing move condition escapes executeMove entirely. Empirically verified on the installed Bun 1.3.13: an uncaught throw in Bun.serve `fetch` yields HTTP 500 and the process survives, but an uncaught throw in `websocket.message` terminates the process (exit=1). Process death drops the socket (ERR_CONNECTION_RESET) and wipes the in-memory `gameSessions` map, so after restart GET /api/game/:id/state and WS upgrade (ws-game.ts:26) return 'Game not found'/404 — exactly the observed asymmetry vs REST.

findings.what: Energy added by Lux's [Add][2] ability is unrestricted; the 'Spend this Energy only to play spells' rider is not enforced.
findings.expected: The 2 energy from Lux should only be usable to pay for spells; with 0 other energy, playUnit for a 2-cost unit should not be legal/offered.
findings.observed: After activating Lux (energy 0->2, all runes still ready), legal moves listed playUnit for every 2-cost unit in hand; executing playUnit on Overzealous Fan (unit, cost 2) succeeded, energy went 2->0 and no runes were exhausted.
findings.reason: Parser output for ven-sp6-006's text "[Exhaust]: [Reaction] — [Add] [2]. Spend this Energy only to play spells." is `{type:"activated", cost:{exhaust:true}, timing:"reaction", effect:{type:"add-resource", energy:2}}` with no restriction (verified by running parseAbilities). riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/activated.ts:263-269 and :361-366 only recognize "Spend this Energy only during showdowns"; the "only to play spells" rider is silently swallowed by the [Add] regex at :272 (`\.?\s*(?:\(.*\))?` doesn't apply, but parseEffects path strips it). Engine handler riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/add-resource.ts:5-10 does `pool.energy += effect.energy` into the generic rune pool with no spend restriction, so the 2 energy pays for any card. Existing test riftbound-engine/src/__tests__/cards/ogs-014-024.test.ts:58 is marked test.failing("BUG: 'Use only to play spells' ...") documenting the same defect for the OGS printing.

findings.what: 'Each player must kill one of their units' resolves as a single choose-target prompt for the controller over ALL units (friendly and enemy), killing exactly one unit total.
findings.expected: Each player separately chooses and kills one of THEIR OWN units: player-1 picks among player-1 units only, player-2 picks among player-2 units only; both kills happen.
findings.observed: pendingChoice {type:choose-target, playerId:player-1, remaining:1, options:[Gem Jammer(p1), Safety Inspector(p1), Recruit token(p2)]}. After p1 picked Gem Jammer, effect ended: p2's Recruit survived, no prompt/auto-kill for player-2. In a second run p1 was able to pick and kill p2's Recruit token instead.
findings.reason: Parser emits {type:"kill", player:"each", target:{type:"unit"}} (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-damage.ts:139-150). The engine never honours player:"each" for kill: game-definition/moves/chain/resolve.ts:160-241 builds a single choose-target for resolved.controller with options = resolveTarget({type:"unit", quantity:"all"}) — no controller filter, so all friendly+enemy units — and remaining:1; abilities/effects/kill.ts handle_kill (lines 8-37) just kills the bound target(s) with no per-player fan-out (unlike discard.ts:18/draw.ts:10/channel.ts:13 which do branch on player==="each"). Result: controller picks one unit from any side, one kill total; opponent never kills their own unit.

findings.what: 'If you paid my additional cost, you don't kill a unit this way' is ignored.
findings.expected: When played with the 3 XP additional cost (triggerEvent.paidAdditionalCost=true), player-1 should not be prompted to kill / should kill nothing; only the opponent kills one of their units.
findings.observed: Played with additionalCostSpec {xp:3} (XP 3->0, paidAdditionalCost:true on the chain item), yet on resolution player-1 still received the same mandatory choose-target kill prompt (options included p1's own Recruit token and Safety Inspector itself) with no way to decline.
findings.reason: Safety Inspector (riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/safety-inspector.ts) has no hand-written abilities, so enrich-cards.ts:30 parses rulesText. Running parseAbilities on the exact rulesText yields only `{type:"kill", player:"each", target:{type:"unit"}}` on trigger play-self — the "If you paid my additional cost, you don't kill a unit this way" clause is dropped entirely (matched by riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-damage.ts:140-150, which emits no condition). On the engine side, riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/kill.ts:8-37 (handle_kill) has no branch for `player: "each"` nor any check of triggerEvent.paidAdditionalCost; it just calls getTargetIds on the generic {type:"unit"} target, producing a single mandatory choose-any-unit prompt for the controller (grep confirms no `player === "each"` handling anywhere in the engine outside channel/draw/discard). Hence paying the 3 XP has no effect on resolution, matching the observed behavior.

findings.what: Effect target selection uses friendly units already on the board instead of units in hand
findings.expected: "You may play a unit from hand" — the caster should be offered the unit cards in their hand (Mischievous Marai / Cemetery Attendant / Dangerous Duo / Windsinger / Immortal Phoenix were in hand) and optionally pick one
findings.observed: playSpell for Here to Help was enumerated only with targets = friendly units on the board (Punching Poro at bf, Flame Chompers in base, Gust Monk at bf); executeMove with a hand unit as target was rejected (no state change). With no friendly unit on board the spell was not castable at all despite 10 energy and 3 units in hand.
findings.reason: Card def (riftbound-cards/src/cards/sfd/here-to-help.ts:15-21) is `{type:"play", from:"hand", target:{controller:"friendly", type:"unit"}}`. play-spell.ts does not special-case play-from-hand: (1) condition at play-spell.ts:235-242 calls spellEffectHasLegalTargets -> targetDescriptorIsSatisfiable -> resolveTarget, which scans only board zones (target-resolver.ts:182 getBoardCardIds = base + battlefields, lines 319-343), so with no friendly unit on board the spell is illegal; (2) enumerator at play-spell.ts:457-471 treats effect.target as a caster-chosen card target and emits one Play per friendly board unit; (3) play-spell.ts:248-267 rejects any supplied targets[0] not in the board pool, so a hand unit target is refused. Only chain/resolve.ts:153-155 exempts `play`+`from:"hand"` from board targeting (at resolution), not the play-time gate/enumerator.

findings.what: Resolution moves an on-board unit for free instead of playing a hand unit at -3 cost to a controlled battlefield
findings.expected: On resolution: chosen unit is played from hand to a battlefield the caster controls, paying its cost reduced by 3 energy; destination limited to controlled battlefields (and to the hidden battlefield when played from facedown, rule 811.1.d.3)
findings.observed: Resolution put a triggered 'move <target> to: choose' item on the chain, then a choose-destination pendingChoice. Normal cast: Flame Chompers (already in base) was moved base -> battlefield, options offered were BOTH battlefields including the uncontrolled enemy one; hand unchanged, no energy/power spent beyond the spell's own cost. From hidden: Gust Monk (already at that battlefield) was auto-selected with no prompt and offered destinations 'base' or the opponent's uncontrolled battlefield; picked base and it moved there. No unit was ever played from hand and no cost reduction occurred. (handle_play in abilities/effects/play.ts ignores from:'hand', reduceCost and toLocation:{battlefield:'controlled'}.)
findings.reason: Card def (riftbound-cards/src/cards/sfd/here-to-help.ts:15-21) declares {type:'play', from:'hand', reduceCost:{energy:3}, toLocation:{battlefield:'controlled'}, target:{controller:'friendly',type:'unit'}}. Engine mishandles all three: (1) play-spell.ts:465-471/567 treats the friendly-unit descriptor as a board card target (no exclusion for play/from:'hand', unlike chain/resolve.ts:155), so cast-time enumeration binds an on-board friendly unit; (2) abilities/effects/play.ts:32 only gathers hand candidates when `from==='hand' && !ctx.boundTargets`, so with the bound board unit it falls to getTargetIds (line 50) and then lines 74-87 push a triggered {type:'move', target, to:'choose'} chain item — toLocation object {battlefield:'controlled'} is neither 'here' nor 'base' so dest='choose' (line 74), no controlled-battlefield restriction; (3) `reduceCost` is never read in play.ts (only referenced in effects/look.ts:38-48), and the move path pays no cost at all. Matches observed: existing unit moved for free with unrestricted destination, hand untouched.

findings.what: Assault 2 not applied to Garen's own Might for lethal-damage/survival when attacking

findings.what: After Charm moves an ENEMY unit onto an uncontrolled battlefield, the Contested status is attributed to the spell's caster (player-1) instead of the moved unit's controller (player-2). Root: pending-choice.ts choose-destination branch calls markContestedOnArrival(draft, targetZoneId, choice.playerId) (and move.ts:220 uses ctx.playerId) — the chooser, not the unit's controller.
findings.expected: Rule 450 / 187.3.a: destination becomes Contested by the controller of the unit that moved (player-2); player-2 gains Focus in the resulting non-combat showdown (rule 345) and, when it closes, player-2 establishes control of Aspirant's Climb.
findings.observed: battlefields['player-2-bf-ogn-276-298'] = {contested:true, contestedBy:'player-1', controller:null}; startShowdown offered to player-1; showdown opened with attackingPlayer:'player-1', focusPlayer:'player-1', isCombatShowdown:true although player-1 has no units there; after both players passed focus the battlefield remained {contested:true, contestedBy:'player-1', controller:null, showdownComplete:true} (player-2 never got control) and a bogus resolveFullCombat move was then offered at a battlefield holding only player-2's Recruit; endTurn was not offered.
findings.reason: Charm ("Move an enemy unit.") parses to {type:"move", target:{controller:"enemy"}, to:"choose"}. abilities/effects/move.ts:256-261 sets pendingChoice {type:"choose-destination", playerId: ctx.playerId} (the caster). On resolution, game-definition/moves/pending-choice.ts:876 calls markContestedOnArrival(draft, targetZoneId, choice.playerId), and move.ts:15-29 writes bf.contestedBy = playerId (and gates on bf.controller === playerId) using that caster id rather than the moved unit's controller. Same pattern at move.ts:220 with ctx.playerId. This violates rule 450 ("Contested ... by the controller of the Unit that moved"), so an enemy unit moved by Charm attributes contestedBy to player-1, matching the observed showdown/focus misattribution.

findings.what: 'When it wins a combat this turn, gain 2 XP.' clause is not implemented — parser output / chain effect for Grim Resolve contains only {type:'modify-might', amount:3, duration:'turn'}; no delayed/turn-scoped win-combat trigger is attached to the buffed unit.
findings.expected: After the buffed Pouty Poro (5 Might) attacked and won combat vs an enemy Recruit (1 Might) at Back-Alley Bar the same turn, player-1 should gain 2 XP (players['player-1'].xp 0 -> 2).
findings.observed: Combat resolved, Recruit killed, player-1 conquered the battlefield (VP 0->1, controller player-1, Poro survived with 0 damage) but players['player-1'].xp stayed 0. Chain item effect was only modify-might; no trigger fired.
findings.reason: Card def /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/grim-resolve.ts:4-16 has no hand-authored `abilities`, so enrich-cards.ts:30 runs parseAbilities on rulesText. Running the parser on the exact rulesText yields a single ability {type:'spell', timing:'action', effect:{type:'modify-might', amount:3, duration:'turn', target:{type:'unit',controller:'friendly'}}} — the "When it wins a combat this turn, gain 2 XP" sentence is silently dropped (spells.ts:170 parseEffects returns only the might buff). The pre-generated data/sets/unl.json:3848 entry likewise has only keyword Action + modify-might. Parser trigger patterns only know "When I win a combat" / "When you win a combat" (trigger-patterns.ts:40,104); there is no "When it wins a combat this turn" delayed-trigger pattern, and no engine special-case for unl-095-219. Hence no win-combat XP trigger is ever attached to the buffed unit and xp stays 0.

findings.what: Second ability "Disempower this, [1], [Exhaust]: Play a 3 [Might] Mech unit token to your base" cannot be activated
findings.expected: With Hextech Disc empowered, ready, and >=1 energy, an activateAbility move (index 1) should be offered; activating should disempower+exhaust the Disc, spend 1 energy, and create a 3-Might Mech token in base
findings.observed: No activateAbility move listed for the Disc in that state (turn 3: empowered=true, exhausted=false, energy 5). Forcing activateAbility abilityIndex:1 via REST returns CONDITION_FAILED. Runtime card def (/api/cards/ven-087-166) shows abilities[1] = {type:"spell", timing:"action", effect:create-token Mech} with NO cost and not type "activated" — the Disempower/[1]/[Exhaust] cost was dropped by the parser, so the engine never exposes it as an activatable ability. No Mech token could ever be produced.
findings.reason: Reproduced: running parseAbilities on Hextech Disc's rulesText yields abilities[1] = {type:"spell", timing:"action", effect:create-token Mech} with no cost. Root cause: packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/activated.ts:205-207 — the leading-text-cost regex only accepts "Disempower me" (`/^(Discard ...|Disempower me)((?:,\s*:rb_...:)*):\s*(.+)$/`), so "Disempower this, [1], [Exhaust]: ..." fails every activated-ability pattern, parseActivatedAbility returns undefined, and parseOtherSegment (other-segment.ts:30-39/66-69) falls through to a costless spell ability. The engine gates activation on ability.type === "activated" (riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/chain/activate-ability.ts:104,145,340), so no activateAbility move is enumerated and forcing it fails. Checked-in ven.json:2715 also has abilities:[null] for this card.

findings.what: "I don't deal combat damage" is not enforced in combat resolution
findings.expected: Ezreal contributes 0 to his side's combat damage (rule text / NoCombatDamage). Attack case: 5-Might enemy Mech with 3 prior damage should survive combat vs lone attacker Ezreal. Defend case: 6-Might attacking Mech with 3 prior damage should survive combat vs lone defender Ezreal.
findings.observed: In both cases the opposing Mech was killed by combat (sent to trash alongside Ezreal), i.e. Ezreal dealt his 3 Might as combat damage. meta.grantedKeywords contains {keyword:"NoCombatDamage",duration:"static"} but packages/riftbound-engine/src/combat/combat-resolver.ts only honours CombatUnit.dealsNoCombatDamage, which is set solely by the Vilemaw PreventWeakerEnemyCombatDamage path — nothing maps the NoCombatDamage keyword onto it.
findings.reason: Card def packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/sfd/ezreal-dashing.ts:49-56 grants keyword "NoCombatDamage" via static grant-keyword. In the engine, calculateSideMight (packages/riftbound-engine/src/combat/combat-resolver.ts:114-121) only skips units with unit.dealsNoCombatDamage. That flag is set in exactly two places: resolve-full-combat.ts:230-234 (stunned units) and combat-resolver.ts:141-143 (Vilemaw PreventWeakerEnemyCombatDamage threshold). A repo-wide grep for "NoCombatDamage" in riftbound-engine/src and apps/riftbound-app finds no other reference — the keyword lands in CombatUnit.keywords but nothing reads it, so Ezreal contributes his full 3 Might to combat damage.

findings.what: Shield's +1 Might is not reflected in Zephyr Sage's current/displayed Might while it is the designated defender in a combat showdown
findings.expected: Per reminder text (+1 Might while I'm a defender) and rule 432.1.a ('A unit with 3 base Might and Shield 2 is in combat as a Defender... its current Might is 5'), Zephyr Sage should show/current-Might 7 while meta.combatRole==='defender'
findings.observed: During the combat showdown (combatRole='defender' confirmed in state) the board card showed no modified-might badge (printed 6), client __rbGameState might=6 and /api state might=6; the attacker's +3 mightModifier DID render as a '6' badge, so the UI folds mightModifier/buff/equipment but not Shield-while-defender (card.js effective-might calc). Shield was only applied inside combat resolution.
findings.reason: render/card.js:199-205 computes effMight = base + meta.mightModifier + meta.staticMightBonus + (buffed?1:0) + equipmentMightBonus — no term for Shield (or Assault) keyed on meta.combatRole, so a Shield defender's badge never changes. Engine-side, Shield is only added inside combat/combat-resolver.ts:96/109 (calculateSideMight / per-unit bonus during resolution) and is never folded into mightModifier/staticMightBonus on the card, so /api state and __rbGameState also report might=6. The only UI place that adds Shield is the combat preview total in gameplay/combat.js:101-104, not the per-card display. Rule 432.1.a states a defending Shield unit's *current* Might includes Shield, so Zephyr Sage should read 7 while combatRole==='defender'.

findings.what: Mode 'Ready 2 runes' does nothing
findings.expected: With 2 friendly runes exhausted, choosing 'Ready 2 runes' should ready both runes
findings.observed: resolvePendingChoice pickedMode=0 succeeded, pendingChoice cleared, but both runes (player-1-rune-4/rune-3) stayed exhausted in server state; no target prompt either. Likely target filter 'exhausted' reads meta.exhausted while exhaustRune stores it in __flags.exhausted, so the rune target set resolves empty and the ready fizzles.
findings.reason: Reproduced with a harness test: two runes exhausted via the real `exhaustRune` move (resources.ts:123 → counters.setFlag writes only cardMeta.__flags.exhausted, core operations-impl.ts:552-558), then equip Svellsongur on Aphelios, chooseMode(0). pendingChoice clears with no target prompt and both runes remain __flags.exhausted=true. Control case with harness-seeded top-level meta.exhausted=true readies both. Root cause: target-resolver.ts:435-436 `case "exhausted": return meta?.exhausted === true` reads the top-level meta field (via raw getCardMeta, operations-impl.ts:350-352), never __flags.exhausted, so the `{type:"rune", filter:"exhausted", quantity:2}` target set (aphelios-exalted.ts:24-29) resolves empty and handle_ready (ready.ts:13-14) fizzles because hasTargetSpec is true. Same mismatch affects `case "ready"` at target-resolver.ts:434 and static-abilities.ts:147/154.

findings.what: 'choose one that hasn't been chosen this turn' not enforced
findings.expected: After picking 'Ready 2 runes' on the first attach this turn, the second attach trigger should offer only the remaining modes (and reject mode 0)
findings.observed: Second and later attach triggers in the same turn still presented options [0,1,2]; picking mode 0 again was accepted. Card meta modesChosenThisTurn stayed unset. handle_choice (abilities/effects/choice.ts) does not copy effect.notChosenThisTurn onto the choose-mode pendingChoice nor filter options by modesChosenThisTurn, so the reducer's recording branch never runs.
findings.reason: abilities/effects/choice.ts:22-30 builds the choose-mode pendingChoice with options = all indices (line 24) and never copies effect.notChosenThisTurn onto it nor reads the source card's modesChosenThisTurn meta. The only consumer, game-definition/moves/pending-choice.ts:636, records modesChosenThisTurn only `if (choice.notChosenThisTurn)` — a field no code path ever sets (grep shows no other writer in engine src). So for sfd-049-221 (aphelios-exalted.ts sets notChosenThisTurn: true on the effect), every attach trigger offers [0,1,2], repeat picks of mode 0 pass the `choice.options.includes(idx)` check at :629, and meta stays unset.

findings.what: 'Buff a friendly unit' gives no target choice
findings.expected: With two friendly units on board (Aphelios already buffed, Shipyard Skulker unbuffed) the player should be prompted to choose which friendly unit to buff
findings.observed: Picking mode 2 resolved immediately with no choose-target pendingChoice; first time it auto-buffed Aphelios, second time (Aphelios already buffed) nothing changed and Skulker was never offered/buffed.
findings.reason: pending-choice.ts:624-660 (choose-mode resolution) calls `executeEffect(picked, effectCtx)` directly on the picked option's effect without raising a choose-target prompt (the choose-target prompt in chain/resolve.ts:141-244 only inspects the top-level effect.target / sequence lead, and a `choice` effect has neither). handle_buff (abilities/effects/buff.ts:22) -> getTargetIds -> resolveTarget, which for a non-"all" quantity returns `filtered.slice(0, 1)` (target-resolver.ts:312-313), i.e. the first friendly unit on board (Aphelios). If that unit is already buffed, buff.ts:29-33 `continue`s, so nothing happens and Skulker is never offered. Matches observed behavior.

findings.what: Temporary granted by Turn to Dust expires at end of turn, so the gear is never killed
findings.expected: Serrated Dirk (given [Temporary] on turn 3) is killed at the start of player-1's next Beginning Phase (turn 5), before scoring
findings.observed: After resolution the gear's meta showed grantedKeywords:[{keyword:'Temporary',duration:'turn'}]; after endTurn the grantedKeywords entry was gone and at turn 5 beginning->main the Serrated Dirk was still in base (trash count unchanged at 1 = the spell itself). The kill never happened.
findings.reason: At HEAD (cbd38e3), packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/grant-keyword.ts:34 is `const duration = (effect.duration ?? "turn")`. The parser emits Turn to Dust's effect as {type:'grant-keyword', keyword:'Temporary', target:{type:'gear'}} with no duration (verified by running parseAbilities on the rulesText), so the grant is recorded with duration:'turn'. riftbound-flow.ts:613-620 (ending phase) then filters out every grantedKeyword with duration === 'turn', so by the controller's next Beginning Phase the Temporary grant is gone and the kill loop at riftbound-flow.ts:274-312 (which checks grantedKeywords for 'Temporary') never matches the Serrated Dirk. This exactly matches the observed meta {keyword:'Temporary',duration:'turn'} disappearing after endTurn. Note: the working tree has an UNCOMMITTED edit at grant-keyword.ts:34-39 defaulting Temporary to 'permanent' (rule 816.1.b) which would fix this, but it is not in HEAD.

findings.what: 'When you play me, ready another friendly Mech' readies nothing even with exhausted friendly Mechs present
findings.expected: On play, an exhausted friendly Mech (sandbox Mech token, or the other exhausted Bubble Bot which is itself a Mech) becomes ready; with 2+ candidates a target prompt is shown
findings.observed: Trigger went on chain as ready{target:{type:unit,controller:friendly,filter:{tag:'Mech'},excludeSelf:true}} with no targets/pendingChoice; after passChainPriority all friendly units (Mech token, Recruit token, first Bubble Bot) stayed exhausted:true. Tested twice: once with an exhausted Mech token, once (via duplicateCard) with an exhausted printed Bubble Bot as the other Mech. Root cause visible in data: target-resolver matches filter.tag against def.tags, but no card def (bubble-bot.ts, mega-mech.ts, etc.) nor the sandbox Mech token def carries tags:['Mech'], so the filter can never match.
findings.reason: Bubble Bot's parsed ability is ready{target:{type:unit,controller:friendly,filter:{tag:"Mech"},excludeSelf:true}} (verified at runtime via getAllCards()). target-resolver.ts:463-465 matches filter.tag strictly against registry def.tags (`return tags?.includes(filter.tag) ?? false`). No card in getAllCards() carries tags containing "Mech" (runtime check: zero matches) — bubble-bot.ts:4-15, mega-mech.ts, breakneck-mech.ts have no `tags`; sfd.json:2348 has "tags": []; sandbox Mech token registration (game-definition/moves/token.ts:133-161) and ability-minted tokens (abilities/effects/create-token.ts:92-98,139-145) register name/might/keywords but no tags. So the filter can never match, targets is empty, and handle_ready (abilities/effects/ready.ts:13-14) fizzles because a target spec exists. Nothing is readied.
